blockingIssues.description: The final decision rail labels a derived policy-vs-actual simulation value as the route's quarterly counterfactual lift while the rest of the route still anchors on the payload/decision-engine lift, so the recommendation packet mixes inconsistent metrics and is not tied to one coherent recommendation rationale.

The recommendation evidence panel remains static (`payload.decisionEvidence`) while nearby decision outputs update from interactive scenario state, so the UI implies scenario-specific rationale that the evidence surface does not actually support.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Clarify in the case-study-worker skill that changes to route-level recommendation calculations or metadata semantics should add or update narrow automated tests before broader validation, not only rely on manual/browser verification.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The ORD-LGA flagship upgrade changed recommendation calculations/presentation without adding route-specific automated coverage; the reviewer traced this to the current skill guidance and the handoff explicitly states that no new automated tests were added.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Clarify in the case-study-worker skill that using an approved dev port for browser validation is acceptable when the production-like manifest port is already occupied and build verification has already passed.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The ORD-LGA worker documented a deviation and suggested this exact clarification after validating on an approved dev port because the shared production-like port could not be safely reclaimed.
